text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Some 80,000 kilogrammes of EU food packages will be the first food aid to Finnish students since World War Two.
- Nuclear power is the best way to protect the environment, says Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto, chairman of the Conservative Party.
- Employer lobbies frustrated about slow progress in reforming the system for companies to pay and borrow back pension contributions.
- Government wants to ensure by law that there will be no speculation with state-subsidised Arava houses which are due to become marketable.
- Healthier diet becoming natural to Finns but lack of physical exercise still causes overweight, study shows.
- Interbank ex-head Juha Sorvisto charged with false written testimony.
- Marble again top candidate material for Finlandia Hall's outer walls.
- Competition has cut many utilities' electricity prices and higher taxes have only partly gone into prices.
KAUPPALEHTI
- International funds are hawling small listed companies shares which are lower valued than the more popular blue-chips.
- There may be changes to Merita's planned options to its management, says chairman of the board Timo Peltola.

- Finns nowadays demand wider product ranges than small daily goods retailers' can offer and large supermarkets are not the main reason for closures, says Jarmo Granfelt, managing director of the Helsinki Institute for Business Studies (LTT).
- Lack of personnel is worsening in the electronics industry, says Tapio Forsgren, chairman of the electronics industry lobby.
AAMULEHTI

- Former president Urho Kekkonen acted in the interest of the country when he blocked former prime minister Ahti Karjalainen's chances of becoming president, says Jukka Seppinen, author of a new book about Karjalainen.

- Finland's aims to keep the Western European Union (WEU) separate from the European Union is becoming a minority position in the face of proposals from Germany and France who want to merge the two, and it may up pressure for Finland to join NATO.
DEMARI
- Parliament plans to start publishing a newsletter.
